title: LTE: Reset RLC & PDCP bearer states opon certain RRC events
description:
This is in response to a capture file received for the issue described at
https://ask.wireshark.org/question/34588/rlc-lte-sequence-analysis-problem/

notes.body: assigned to @martin.r.mathieson

Yes they are reset, so it is worth calling PDCP also. note that a LTE UE can use a NR PDCP entoty instead of a LTE PDCP entity. This is  not supported by the RLC and RRC LTE dissectors and probably deserve a specific MR.

changed this line in [version 3 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/16110/diffs?diff_id=1046554427&start_sha=3c8896dfc0478f7a7ec345dc433be9e78554ceab#d4d413d8d4cdc4b48154bc9780f00e094982d2eb_2445_2452)
Not going to try to support NR PDCP case here.

I think we should also reset the RLC/PDCP entities in case of rrcEarlyDataRequest-r15. In case of rrcConnectionReestablishmentRequest, the RLC entities are reset, and the PDCP UM and SRB are reset while the PDCP AM are not (like during a handover). The rrcConnectionResumeRequest-r13 is even more complex as the transmission is done on SRB1 even if it is a UL CCCH message, and with SN=0...

The same changes must be applied for the NB-IoT case also.
Am now trying to do appropriate resets for all entry points, but not attempting PDCP handling of rrcConnectionResumeRequest-r13 in this MR.
Going to merge with current handling and TODOs
